name: ftdi-jtag-scan
experiment:
# FTDI/MPSSE JTAG adapter through the NATIVE Go stack (Linux usbfs ->
# FTDI protocol -> MPSSE -> JTAG TAP). No OpenOCD, no Python, no libusb.
#
# Recorded on a REAL Sipeed RV-Debugger-BL702 (an FT2232D emulator, USB
# 0403:6010 "SIPEED JTAG Debugger"). Only USB interface 0 is claimed; the
# companion UART (interface 1, /dev/ttyUSBx) stays with the kernel and the
# uart plugin. See docs/notes/phase16-ftdi-mpsse-jtag-results.md.
#
#   hwlab devices                       # ftdi/0403:6010:<serial>
#   hwlab run examples/ftdi-jtag-scan.yaml
#
# Every step is safe: TAP reset, a clock-less sync probe, a loopback check and
# an IDCODE/BYPASS enumeration. Nothing is written to a target. With no target
# on the JTAG pins the scan correctly reports status "no-device".
#
# For a SYNTHETIC adapter with one fabricated Cortex-M-like TAP (no hardware):
#   HWLAB_FTDI_SIM=1 hwlab run examples/ftdi-jtag-sim.yaml
name: ftdi-jtag-scan
duration: 3s

devices:
  jtag:
    plugin: ftdi

steps:
  - {name: adapter-info, at: 100ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGTransport.info}
  - {name: selftest, at: 300ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGTransport.selftest}
  - {name: tap-reset, at: 500ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGTransport.tap_reset}
  - {name: scan-1, at: 700ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGScan.scan, args: {measure_ir: true}}
  - {name: scan-2, at: 1000ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGScan.scan, args: {measure_ir: true}}
  - {name: scan-3, at: 1300ms, device: jtag, call: JTAGScan.scan, args: {measure_ir: true}}
  - {name: identify, at: 1600ms, device: jtag, call: TargetIdentify.identify}
